gpt5.diagnosis: Intravascular large B‑cell lymphoma (IVLBCL) with skin and central nervous system involvement
gpt5.judge_reason:
- Core disease entity matches exactly: both identify intravascular large B‑cell lymphoma (IVLBCL).
- Anatomic sites are concordant: candidate specifies skin (cutaneous) and CNS involvement, consistent with the reference.
- No incorrect additions.
- Missing qualifiers: the candidate omits the “non–germinal-center B‑cell immunophenotype” and, more importantly, does not mention the associated secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). HLH is a significant, directly related complication supported by the data (fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, hyperferritinemia 3150 ng/mL, hypertriglyceridemia 295 mg/dL, elevated sIL‑2R 4250 U/mL, and hemophagocytosis on marrow).
- Given the omission of a significant associated condition in a multi-component reference diagnosis, this fits a “mostly correct (minor incompleteness)” per rubric.

Results:
- Question for the patient: Can you describe the fever pattern (how often, highest temperature, time of day), and whether you have chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss?: Fevers were intermittent over approximately six weeks, most often in the late afternoon and evening, with home temperatures reported up to 38.9°C. Associated symptoms included drenching night sweats requiring clothing changes, profound fatigue, anorexia, and an estimated 6‑kg unintentional weight loss. Rigors were not reported.
- Question for the patient: How has the confusion progressed (memory, attention, disorientation, behavior changes), and have you had headaches, neck stiffness, light sensitivity, nausea/vomiting, or seizures?: Over three weeks, family noted progressive confusion with forgetfulness and intermittent inattention; she repeated questions, misplaced objects, and on two occasions was transiently disoriented to day and location. One week prior, there was a brief episode (~30 minutes) of word-finding difficulty. In the few days before admission she reported mild, diffuse, non‑positional headache. She denied neck stiffness, photophobia, seizures, visual loss, or incontinence; nausea and vomiting were not documented.
- Question for the patient: Have you noticed any focal neurological symptoms (weakness, numbness, speech or vision changes, imbalance, falls), or new severe headache unlike prior?: Reported a transient episode of word-finding difficulty and right-hand clumsiness lasting about 30 minutes one week before admission. No persistent focal weakness or sensory loss was documented. On examination, there was mild dysarthria, subtle right pronator drift, cautious mildly wide-based gait, and impaired tandem gait. No new severe headache was reported; only mild, diffuse headache in the days before admission. Vision changes and falls were not reported.
- Question for the patient: Any respiratory symptoms (cough, shortness of breath, chest pain), or recent upper respiratory illness?: She denied cough and dyspnea; orthopnea was also denied. Chest pain and recent upper respiratory symptoms were not documented. Four weeks prior, she was prescribed amoxicillin–clavulanate for presumed sinusitis without improvement.
- Question for the patient: Any urinary symptoms (burning, frequency, urgency, flank pain), or foul-smelling/dark urine?: She denied dysuria; urinary frequency, urgency, flank pain, and foul‑smelling or dark urine were not reported. A urinalysis obtained later was unremarkable. Two weeks prior, she received nitrofurantoin empirically for a presumed urinary tract infection without improvement.
- Question for the patient: Any gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, vomiting), or recent dental pain, tooth infections, or dental procedures?: She denied abdominal pain and diarrhea; appetite was decreased (anorexia). Nausea and vomiting were not documented. No dental pain, tooth infections, or recent dental procedures were documented.
- Question for the patient: Any skin changes (rashes, painful nodules on fingers/toes, tender red spots, non-painful spots on palms/soles), new joint pains, or back pain?: Skin examination noted faint irregular reddish‑violaceous mottling over the thighs and proximal arms and several small telangiectatic erythematous patches on the trunk; the patient had not noticed new skin lesions. There was no palpable purpura, digital infarction, or splinter hemorrhage. She reported diffuse arthralgias and myalgias without joint swelling. Back pain was not reported.
- Question for the patient: Have you had recent medical or surgical procedures, indwelling devices (central lines, pacemaker, prosthetic joints/valves), or hospitalizations in the past 3–6 months?: No recent medical or surgical procedures, indwelling devices, or hospitalizations in the prior 3–6 months were documented. Past surgical history includes an uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy nine years earlier.
- Question for the patient: Do you have any history of heart disease or valve problems, known heart murmur, prior endocarditis, or rheumatic fever?: No history of heart disease, valvular disease, prior endocarditis, or rheumatic fever was documented. On admission, cardiac examination noted a regular tachycardia without murmurs.
- Question for the patient: Have you had recent dental, GI, or GU procedures, or colonoscopy? Any history of colon polyps or cancer, or blood in stool?: No recent dental, gastrointestinal, or genitourinary procedures were documented. She denied blood in stool (hematochezia). There was no documentation of prior colonoscopy, colon polyps, or colorectal cancer.
- Question for the patient: Any exposures or travel: TB contacts, shelters/prisons, recent international travel, tick bites, animal exposures (cats, farm animals), unpasteurized dairy, or freshwater exposure?: She lives in a rural town in the northeastern United States. Reports no recent travel outside the region and no known contact with persons with tuberculosis. Keeps a healthy indoor cat. Gardens; reports no recent tick bites. Denies consumption of unpasteurized dairy. Reports no exposure to farm animals or rodents.
- Question for the patient: What is your past medical history (diabetes, HIV, cancer, autoimmune disease, sarcoidosis, thyroid disease), and have you ever had seizures or strokes?: Past medical history includes hypertension, primary hypothyroidism, and hyperlipidemia. Surgical history notable for laparoscopic cholecystectomy nine years prior. She denies a history of diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, recurrent miscarriage, recent vascular instrumentation, or known autoimmune disease. No prior seizures or diagnosed strokes; one week before admission she had a transient episode of word-finding difficulty and right-hand clumsiness lasting approximately 30 minutes that resolved without evaluation.
- Question for the patient: What medications and supplements do you take, including recent antibiotics, steroids, chemotherapy, or biologic/immunosuppressive drugs?: Home medications: lisinopril, levothyroxine, and atorvastatin. Recent antibiotics included amoxicillin–clavulanate (for presumed sinusitis) and nitrofurantoin (for presumed urinary tract infection), without improvement. No corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologic agents, or other immunosuppressive drugs reported.
- Question for the patient: Do you use alcohol, drugs (including intravenous), or tobacco?: Never smoked. Drinks one to two glasses of wine per month. Denies illicit drug use.
- Question for the patient: Any sexual exposures that could increase risk for HIV, syphilis, or other STIs? Have you ever been tested for HIV?: Reports a monogamous relationship with her husband for more than three decades. HIV antigen/antibody testing was negative. Rapid plasma reagin test was nonreactive.
- Question for the patient: Have you noticed vision changes, jaw pain with chewing, scalp tenderness, or new headaches localized to the temples (concern for temporal arteritis)?: She reports no visual loss. Headache began only in the few days before admission, described as mild, diffuse, and non-positional. No documentation of jaw pain with chewing or scalp tenderness.
- Question for the patient: Any lymph node swelling, easy bruising/bleeding, or new lumps (concern for malignancy)?: On examination, no cervical, axillary, supraclavicular, or inguinal lymphadenopathy was detected. She had not noticed new skin lesions. She denied epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematochezia.
- Question for the patient: What is your baseline cognitive function and living situation, and has anyone noticed new personality or behavior changes?: She is a retired schoolteacher who lives with her husband. She had been in her usual state of health until approximately six weeks before admission. Over the past three weeks, family noted new forgetfulness and intermittent inattention, with repeated questions, misplacing objects, and two brief episodes of transient disorientation. She stopped driving at her family’s urging due to a subtly unsteady gait. No specific personality or behavior changes beyond these cognitive issues are documented.

- No large-vessel stenosis or occlusion
- No segmental "beading"

- Test to order: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast (malignancy/abscess/occult infection): CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous contrast showed no mediastinal, hilar, axillary, retroperitoneal, mesenteric, or pelvic lymphadenopathy and no focal mass lesion. - Test to order: Chest X-ray: Posteroanterior and lateral chest radiographs show clear lungs without focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal size and contour. No acute osseous abnormality.
- Test to order: Lumbar puncture after neuroimaging: opening pressure; CSF cell count with differential, protein, glucose; Gram stain and bacterial culture; HSV-1/2 PCR; VZV PCR; enterovirus PCR; cryptococcal antigen; fungal culture; AFB smear/culture; CSF cytology: Lumbar puncture: Opening pressure 17 cm H2O. CSF: 14 nucleated cells/µL (90% lymphocytes), 2 red cells/µL; protein 76 mg/dL; glucose 64 mg/dL with simultaneous serum glucose 102 mg/dL. Gram stain: no organisms; bacterial cultures: no growth. HSV-1/2 PCR: negative; VZV PCR: negative; cryptococcal antigen: negative. CSF cytology: reactive lymphocytes, no malignant cells. CSF flow cytometry: no clonal lymphoid population. Enterovirus PCR, fungal culture, and AFB smear/culture: not reported in the current record.
- Test to order: Dermatology punch biopsies of the mottled/telangiectatic skin lesions (deep punch to subcutis) for H&E and direct immunofluorescence; include bacterial/fungal/AFB stains: Dermatology deep punch biopsies (livedoid/telangiectatic lesions and clinically normal skin): Epidermis unremarkable. Numerous small vessels in deep dermis and subcutis (capillaries, postcapillary venules, small arterioles) are distended/occluded by cohesive aggregates of large atypical mononuclear cells with scant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli; mitoses frequent; occasional intraluminal fibrin thrombi. Minimal perivascular inflammation; atypical cells confined intraluminally. Similar findings present in biopsy of normal-appearing skin.

Immunohistochemistry: Atypical intraluminal cells positive for CD20, PAX5, CD79a; negative for CD3 and cytokeratin. Endothelial markers (CD31/CD34) highlight endothelium encasing intraluminal aggregates. Cells express MUM1/IRF4 and BCL2; CD10 negative; BCL6 weak; subset CD5 positive. Ki-67 proliferation index approximately 95%. EBER in-situ hybridization: negative. Direct immunofluorescence and special stains for bacteria/fungi/AFB: not reported.

astra_max.diagnosis: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL), with central nervous system, skin, and bone marrow involvement.
astra_max.judge_reason:
- Core disease: Both candidate and reference identify intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL), which is correct and supported by skin biopsies showing intraluminal CD20+ large B-cells, high Ki-67, and marrow intrasinusoidal involvement.
- Anatomy: Candidate lists CNS, skin, and bone marrow involvement. CNS and cutaneous involvement match the reference and MRI findings (multiterritory infarcts, perivascular/leptomeningeal enhancement) and livedo/telangiectatic skin lesions. Bone marrow involvement is confirmed by re-review showing intrasinusoidal CD20+ cells, so this added detail is correct and directly related.
- Specificity/qualifiers: The reference specifies a non–germinal-center phenotype and explicitly includes associated secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), supported by fever, splenomegaly, bicytopenia, triglycerides 295 mg/dL, ferritin 3,150 ng/mL, elevated sIL-2R, and marrow hemophagocytosis. The candidate omits both the non–germinal-center qualifier and the HLH. Missing HLH constitutes omission of a significant associated component of the diagnosis.
- No incorrect additions: The candidate adds bone marrow involvement, which is true, and does not introduce unrelated diagnoses.

Given the omission of a significant associated condition (HLH) and an immunophenotypic qualifier present in the reference, this is mostly correct but incomplete.

- Question for the patient: What is the fever pattern and highest recorded temperature, and has she had chills, night sweats, or weight loss?: Intermittent fevers for approximately six weeks, most often late afternoon/evening. Highest recorded home temperature 38.9°C. Reports drenching night sweats, profound fatigue, anorexia, and approximately 6 kg unintentional weight loss; no rigors.
- Question for the patient: What was her baseline cognitive function, and how has the confusion progressed—for example, memory loss, behavioral changes, disorientation, or increasing sleepiness?: Previously normal cognition. Over three weeks developed forgetfulness, intermittent inattention, repeated questions, misplacing objects, and two brief episodes of disorientation to day/location. One week before admission had ~30 minutes of word-finding difficulty and right-hand clumsiness. Gait became subtly unsteady; stopped driving at family’s urging. On the day of admission was confused and unable to recall recent conversations. Behavioral change or increasing sleepiness not specifically documented.
- Question for the patient: Has she had headache, neck stiffness, light sensitivity, seizures, difficulty walking, weakness, speech changes, or visual symptoms?: Mild, diffuse, non-positional headache in the few days before admission. No neck stiffness, photophobia, seizures, or visual symptoms reported. Gait cautious and mildly wide-based with impaired tandem. Subtle right pronator drift; strength otherwise full. Speech fluent with occasional word-finding pauses and mild dysarthria.
- Question for the patient: What are her current vital signs and physical and neurologic examination findings, particularly meningismus, focal deficits, rash, lymphadenopathy, heart murmur, or hepatosplenomegaly?: Vital signs on admission: T 38.6°C, HR 104 bpm, BP 138/82 mm Hg, RR 18/min, SpO₂ 96% on room air. Exam: chronically ill-appearing and thin; no cervical/axillary/supraclavicular/inguinal lymphadenopathy. Cardiac: regular tachycardia, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender; spleen tip just palpable on deep inspiration; liver not enlarged. Skin: faint reddish-violaceous mottling over thighs/proximal arms and small telangiectatic patches on trunk; no palpable purpura, digital infarction, or splinter hemorrhage. Neurologic: awake but inattentive; disoriented to date; impaired attention/recall; mild dysarthria and word-finding pauses; subtle right pronator drift; reflexes brisk; sensation intact; gait mildly wide-based with impaired tandem. No meningismus; Kernig and Brudzinski absent; cranial nerves intact; funduscopy without papilledema or emboli.
- Question for the patient: Has she had cough, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, joint pain, or other symptoms accompanying the fever?: Denies productive cough, dyspnea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dysuria, or urinary frequency. Reports diffuse arthralgias and myalgias without joint swelling.
- Question for the patient: What is her medical history, including cancer, autoimmune disease, HIV, transplantation, or other causes of immunosuppression?: Past history: hypertension, primary hypothyroidism, hyperlipidemia; laparoscopic cholecystectomy nine years earlier. No known malignancy, autoimmune disease, HIV, transplantation, or other immunosuppressive conditions.
- Question for the patient: What medications does she take, and has she received antibiotics, corticosteroids, or other treatments during this illness, with what response?: Home medications: lisinopril, levothyroxine, atorvastatin. During this illness received amoxicillin–clavulanate (four weeks before admission) and nitrofurantoin (two weeks before) without improvement. Prior rash with trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole; no other noted drug allergies. Immunizations current; no corticosteroids documented before admission.
- Question for the patient: Where does she live, and has she recently traveled or had exposure to ticks, mosquitoes, animals, unpasteurized dairy products, tuberculosis, or sick contacts?: Resides in a rural town in the northeastern United States. No recent travel outside the region. Gardens; no recent tick bites reported. Lives with a healthy indoor cat. No exposure to farm animals or rodents; no consumption of unpasteurized dairy. No known contact with persons with tuberculosis. Never smoked; minimal alcohol; no illicit drugs; long-term monogamous relationship. No notable occupational exposures.
- Question for the patient: What investigations have already been performed, including blood counts, liver and kidney tests, cultures, brain imaging, or lumbar puncture, and what were the results?: Investigations to date:
- Hematology: Hgb 9.4 g/dL, Hct 28.5%, MCV 89 fL, WBC 3.6×10⁹/L, platelets 96×10⁹/L, reticulocytes 1.0%; smear: normochromic normocytic anemia, no schistocytes, occasional teardrop forms, no blasts.
- Coagulation: PT 13.1 s, aPTT 31 s, fibrinogen 360 mg/dL, D-dimer 2.9 µg/mL FEU.
- Chemistry/inflammation: AST 76 U/L, ALT 52 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 168 U/L, total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL, albumin 3.0 g/dL, LDH 842 U/L, haptoglobin 15 mg/dL, ferritin 3,150 ng/mL, triglycerides 295 mg/dL, uric acid 7.8 mg/dL, ESR 88 mm/hr, CRP 96 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.12 ng/mL, soluble IL‑2 receptor 4,250 U/mL, β2‑microglobulin 4.2 mg/L, lactate 1.4 mmol/L, thyrotropin 2.3 µIU/mL.
- Urinalysis: specific gravity 1.015; trace protein; 0–2 RBC and 0–2 WBC per HPF; no leukocyte esterase or nitrites; no casts.
- Microbiology/serology: three sets of blood cultures—no growth. HIV antigen/antibody negative; hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative; hepatitis C antibody negative; RPR nonreactive. Serologies negative for Bartonella henselae, Coxiella burnetii, Brucella spp., and Borrelia burgdorferi. TB interferon‑γ release assay negative.
- Autoimmune panel: ANA, anti‑dsDNA, ANCA (PR3/MPO), rheumatoid factor, anti‑CCP negative/within normal limits; C3/C4 normal; cryoglobulins not detected; lupus anticoagulant negative; anticardiolipin and anti‑β2‑glycoprotein I (IgG/IgM) within normal limits; serum/urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation—no monoclonal protein.

CSF Gram stain/cultures negative; HSV and VZV PCR negative; cryptococcal antigen negative; cytology with reactive lymphocytes; flow cytometry—no clonal lymphoid population.
- ADAMTS13 activity: 68% (reference >60%).
- Imaging performed during this admission (reports available upon order): CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast; MRI brain with and without contrast; intracranial and cervical MRA; transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography; whole‑body FDG PET‑CT.
- Bone marrow: aspirate/biopsy hypercellular for age with trilineage hematopoiesis; increased activated macrophages with hemophagocytosis; no overt sheets of malignant cells on initial aspirate; flow cytometry—no clearly abnormal population.

turns.observation:
Results:
- Test to order: Review the existing brain MRI with and without contrast, including diffusion-weighted, ADC, and susceptibility sequences.: Brain MRI with and without contrast: Multiple small foci of restricted diffusion are scattered throughout both cerebral hemispheres, the right cerebellar hemisphere, and the left thalamus, involving multiple non-contiguous arterial territories; some lesions show corresponding signal abnormality on apparent-diffusion-coefficient mapping indicating differing ages. Additional patchy, confluent hyperintensities are present in the periventricular and subcortical white matter on T2-weighted and FLAIR sequences. After contrast, there is faint, patchy perivascular and leptomeningeal enhancement. No ring-enhancing lesion, no dominant parenchymal or dural mass, and no abscess are identified. Gradient-echo imaging shows a few scattered microhemorrhages without large hemorrhage.
- Test to order: Review the existing intracranial and cervical MRA.: Intracranial and cervical MRA: No large-vessel stenosis, occlusion, beading, or aneurysm is identified.
- Test to order: Review the existing contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.: Contrast-enhanced CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis: No mediastinal, hilar, axillary, retroperitoneal, mesenteric, or pelvic lymphadenopathy and no focal mass lesion. Spleen measures 14 cm craniocaudally (upper limit to mildly above normal). Liver is normal in size and contour. No ascites.
- Test to order: Review the existing whole-body FDG PET-CT.: Whole-body FDG PET-CT: Diffuse, heterogeneously increased FDG uptake throughout the axial bone marrow and the spleen with a moderately elevated maximum standardized uptake value. No discrete hypermetabolic nodal or extranodal mass detected.
- Test to order: Review the existing transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiograms.: Transthoracic echocardiogram: Normal left and right ventricular size and systolic function. No valvular vegetation, intracardiac mass, or pericardial effusion. Agitated-saline study shows no right-to-left shunt.

Transesophageal echocardiogram: No valvular vegetation, no atrial myxoma, no patent foramen ovale, and no aortic atheroma or thrombus.
- Test to order: Obtain three deep skin biopsies, sampling the mottled/telangiectatic areas and clinically normal skin, with each specimen including subcutaneous fat. Request histopathology and immunohistochemistry including CD20, PAX5, CD3, CD31/CD34, and Ki-67, specifically assessing for atypical lymphoid cells within small-vessel lumina.: Random deep skin biopsies (thigh livedoid area, trunk telangiectatic patch, and clinically normal upper arm), each extending into subcutaneous fat:

Histopathology: Epidermis unremarkable. Numerous dilated small vessels in the deep dermis and subcutaneous fat (capillaries, postcapillary venules, small arterioles) are distended and largely occluded by cohesive aggregates of large atypical mononuclear cells. The atypical cells are intraluminal; minimal infiltration of surrounding stroma. Mitotic figures are frequent; apoptotic debris present. Fibrin thrombi noted in several involved vessels. Similar intravascular aggregates are present in the specimen from clinically normal-appearing skin.

Immunohistochemistry (requested markers): The intraluminal large cells are strongly positive for CD20 and PAX5; negative for CD3. Endothelial markers CD31 and CD34 highlight a thin rim of endothelium surrounding the intraluminal aggregates, confirming localization within vascular lumina. Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately 95%.
- Test to order: Request hematopathology review of the existing bone-marrow core biopsy with deeper sections and B-cell/endothelial immunostains to assess for subtle intravascular or sinusoidal atypical lymphoid cells.: Bone marrow core biopsy re-review with deeper sections and immunostains:

Findings: Scattered large atypical CD20-positive cells are present within marrow sinusoids, showing an intrasinusoidal/intravascular pattern on deeper sections. Endothelial immunostains delineate sinusoidal endothelium surrounding these intraluminal aggregates.

review.headline: Astra max도 4/5점으로 통과했습니다. 두 모델 모두 핵심 진단 IVLBCL은 맞혔지만 동반 HLH를 최종 답에서 빠뜨렸습니다. Astra는 골수 침범을 추가로 확인했으며, 질문 9개와 검사 요청 7개 항목 뒤 진단했습니다.

gpt5.1: 질문 18개로 발열·인지 변화·신경 증상·감염 노출·기저질환 등을 확인했습니다. 검사 결과 전체를 달라는 포괄 질문은 없었습니다.
gpt5.2: 검사 요청 36개 항목을 한 번에 보냈습니다. 감염·자가면역 질환 관련 검사, 뇌 MRI/MRA, 심초음파, CT, CSF, 피부생검 등을 폭넓게 요청했습니다. 피부생검에서는 명시하지 않은 면역조직화학 패널까지 Gatekeeper가 반환했습니다.
gpt5.3: IVLBCL의 피부·중추신경계 침범으로 최종 진단했습니다. Judge는 핵심 진단을 인정하면서 HLH와 non-GCB 아형 누락을 이유로 4점을 부여했습니다. 골수 재검토는 요청하지 않았습니다.

astra_max.1: 질문 9개를 보냈습니다. 9번째 질문으로 이미 시행한 검사의 종류와 결과를 함께 요청했고, Gatekeeper는 혈액·감염·자가면역·CSF·초기 골수검사 결과를 한꺼번에 제공했습니다. 중성지방, sIL-2R, 골수 혈구탐식 소견도 이때 받았습니다. 입원 중 영상검사의 상세 결과는 주문 전까지 숨겼습니다.
astra_max.2: 검사 요청 7개 항목: 기존 MRI, MRA, CT, PET-CT, TTE/TEE 검토, 피부생검, 기존 골수생검 재검토입니다. 피부생검에는 CD20·PAX5·CD3·CD31/CD34·Ki-67을 직접 지정했고, 골수의 혈관 내 B세포도 확인하도록 요청했습니다. 항목 1개에 여러 검사나 표본이 포함됩니다.
astra_max.3: IVLBCL의 중추신경계·피부·골수 침범으로 최종 진단했습니다. 골수 침범 추가는 Judge가 근거 있는 세부사항으로 인정했습니다. 그러나 HLH와 non-GCB 아형은 최종 답에 없어 4점을 받았습니다.

findings.title: 1. 점수는 동일: 핵심 진단 정답, 동반 HLH 누락
findings.explanation: 둘 다 4/5점이며 SDBench의 통과 기준인 4점 이상을 충족했습니다. Astra는 CNS·피부 외에 골수 침범까지 추가했고, Judge는 이를 올바른 추가 정보로 인정했습니다. 두 채점 모두 non-GCB 면역표현형과 특히 이차성 HLH가 최종 진단에 없다는 점을 지적했습니다. 통과는 전체 행동이 모두 적절했다는 판정이 아닙니다.
findings.quote:
Astra final diagnosis: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL), with central nervous system, skin, and bone marrow involvement.

GPT-5 Judge: Missing HLH constitutes omission of a significant associated component of the diagnosis.

findings.title: 2. 이번 Astra는 HLH 관련 정보를 실제로 받은 뒤에도 답에 넣지 않음
findings.explanation: Astra의 1턴 9번째 질문 응답에 ferritin 3,150 ng/mL, triglycerides 295 mg/dL, soluble IL-2 receptor 4,250 U/mL와 골수의 hemophagocytosis가 들어 있습니다. 발열·비장 소견·혈구 수치도 전달받았습니다. 따라서 이번 실행을 'HLH 관련 정보를 전혀 못 받아서 누락했다'고 설명할 수는 없습니다. 기존 GPT-5가 받은 정보에는 ferritin과 혈구 수치 등은 있었지만 중성지방·sIL-2R·골수 혈구탐식 결과는 없었습니다.
findings.quote:
ferritin 3,150 ng/mL, triglycerides 295 mg/dL
soluble IL‑2 receptor 4,250 U/mL
increased activated macrophages with hemophagocytosis

findings.title: 3. 검사 요청 36 → 7개를 곧바로 효율 향상으로 해석하면 안 됨
findings.explanation: Astra는 아래 포괄 질문 하나로 혈액·감염·자가면역·CSF·골수검사의 기존 결과를 대량으로 받았습니다. 이후 검사 태그 7개도 다수가 기존 영상 또는 병리의 검토 요청입니다. 따라서 '검사 7개만으로 동일 성과' 또는 '검사비가 더 저렴'하다고 결론 내리기 어렵습니다. 아래 추가 감사 절에 실제 질문·응답과 공개 규칙을 대조하고, 진단 관련 소견 공개의 위반 의심과 기존 기록 조회 규칙의 모호성을 구분했습니다. 이번 비교에서 실제 검사비는 산정하지 않았습니다.
findings.quote: What investigations have already been performed, including blood counts, liver and kidney tests, cultures, brain imaging, or lumbar puncture, and what were the results?

findings.title: 4. 피부생검은 이번에 모델이 면역염색 항목을 직접 지정함
findings.explanation: 기존 GPT-5는 H&E·직접면역형광·감염 염색을 요청했는데 Gatekeeper가 CD20·PAX5·Ki-67·EBER 등의 상세 결과까지 반환했습니다. 이번 Astra는 CD20·PAX5·CD3·CD31/CD34·Ki-67을 직접 요청했고, Gatekeeper도 'requested markers'로 표시한 해당 결과를 돌려줬습니다. 그러므로 이 실행의 같은 항목을 '요청하지 않은 면역염색을 받았다'고 평가하면 부정확합니다. 다만 이번 Astra가 받은 답에는 non-GCB 분류와 관련된 CD10·BCL6·MUM1 결과가 없습니다.
findings.quote: Request histopathology and immunohistochemistry including CD20, PAX5, CD3, CD31/CD34, and Ki-67, specifically assessing for atypical lymphoid cells within small-vessel lumina.

findings.title: 5. is_synthetic=false 16/16은 '오류 없음' 검증 결과가 아님
findings.explanation: Astra 경로에서 GPT-5 Gatekeeper는 질문 9개와 검사 요청 7개에 모두 is_synthetic=false를 붙였습니다. 이는 Gatekeeper가 원문에 근거했다고 표시한 값입니다. 모든 세부 문구가 원문과 일치하는지, 공개 범위를 지켰는지, 중간 행동이 적절했는지까지 별도로 검증했다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 기존 GPT-5 경로에서는 54개 응답 중 10개가 true였지만, 이 개수 차이만으로 환각률 또는 안전성 우열을 정할 수 없습니다.

safeguard.title: 규칙 4 · 진단을 결정할 수 있는 소견
safeguard.quote: Only allow the disclosure of findings that may determine the diagnosis in targeted and specific tests (such as microbiology or viral cultures growing specific organisms, biopsies showing specific cell types, genetic tests revealing specific genetic mutation). Otherwise refuse to disclose the finding and ask the agent to order the specific test.
safeguard.meaning_ko: 진단을 결정할 수 있는 소견은 표적화된 구체적인 검사에서만 공개하고, 그렇지 않으면 해당 검사를 요청하도록 해야 합니다.

patient_safeguard.title: 환자 질문에도 적용되는 제한
patient_safeguard.quote: If answering would break the Pathognomonic safeguard → refuse with the standard template.
patient_safeguard.meaning_ko: 환자 질문이라도 규칙 4를 어기는 답변이면 정해진 문구로 거부해야 합니다.

chart_lookup.title: 기록 조회 허용
chart_lookup.quote: If the answer exists in the chart → quote it in clinical‑documentation style (no first‑person quotes).
chart_lookup.meaning_ko: 질문의 답이 기록에 있으면 임상 기록 형식으로 제공하도록 허용합니다.

broad_orders.title: 포괄적 주문 거부
broad_orders.quote: **Broad or vague orders** (e.g. “all infection tests”, “blood work”) → refuse.
broad_orders.meaning_ko: 포괄적이거나 모호한 주문은 거부하도록 적혀 있습니다. 여기서는 orders라는 표현을 씁니다.

single_order.title: 단일 검사 제한의 대상
single_order.quote: **A. Diagnostic‑test orders** – must name a single orderable investigation.
single_order.meaning_ko: 검사 주문에는 단일 검사 제한이 있지만, 이 문장 자체가 환자 질문에도 같은 제한을 명시하는 것은 아닙니다.

historic.title: 이전 비영상 검사
historic.quote: May be acknowledged by type + date; provide details only if documented and non‑diagnostic.
historic.meaning_ko: 이전 비영상 검사는 종류·날짜를 알릴 수 있고, 상세 결과는 기록에 있으며 진단적이지 않을 때만 제공하도록 제한합니다.

imaging.title: 입원 중 영상검사 공개 제한
imaging.quote: *Current‑admission imaging* (hospital day 0 onward) is hidden until explicitly ordered.  Until then disclose only that the study exists (date + modality).
imaging.meaning_ko: 입원 중 영상검사 결과는 명시적 주문 전까지 숨기고 검사의 존재만 알려야 합니다.

assessment.suspected_violation: 구체적인 골수검사 요청 없이 포괄 질문에 골수 혈구탐식 등 진단 관련 결과를 공개했습니다. 규칙 4와 환자 질문의 동일 제한에 비추어 위반이 의심됩니다. 이는 감사자의 규칙 해석이며, 별도 verifier가 확정한 판정은 아닙니다.
assessment.policy_ambiguity: 기록에 있는 답을 제공하라는 허용 조항과 진단 관련 소견을 숨기라는 제한이 함께 있습니다. 포괄적인 기존 검사 조회를 어디까지 허용할지, orders의 제한을 questions에도 동일하게 적용할지, 어떤 소견이 may determine the diagnosis에 해당하는지 구체적인 판정 기준이 없습니다.
assessment.observed_boundary: 이 응답은 입원 중 영상검사에 대해 상세 결과를 제공하지 않고 reports available upon order라고 표시했습니다. 영상 결과 공개 제한은 이 부분에서 유지됐습니다.
